title: Detection of Identify Roles
summary: This strategy detects the collection of employee roles and responsibilities, ATT&CK sub technique T1591.004, which adversaries use to choose targets for phishing, help desk impersonation and business email compromise. The adversary looks for names, job titles, team structures, reporting lines and contact details on professional networking sites, company pages, conference agendas and job postings. Detectable telemetry comes from identity and directory services rather than the endpoint: search and profile view records in the identity provider or employee directory, bulk query patterns from a single account, outbound web requests to professional networking and people search domains, and email gateway logs showing directory style harvesting. Detection is built around behaviour that a normal employee never generates, such as an authenticated account enumerating the directory far beyond its role, or an external source resolving a large number of staff addresses in one session. The strategy fails because directory searches are among the most common actions in any company, because recruiting and sales teams query these sources legitimately every day, and because an unauthenticated adversary can learn most of it from public data without touching any of your systems.

beginner.definition: Attackers want to know who works at your company and what each person does. A name and a job title is enough to write a believable message. This detection looks for unusual searching of your staff directory and for bulk lookups of people on public sites. It catches the research step before the phishing starts.
beginner.whyItMatters: A phishing email that names your manager and your project is far more convincing than a generic one. Attackers also look for the person who resets passwords, because that role can unlock accounts. Knowing the team structure tells them who reports to whom and who is likely to trust whom. This research is cheap, and it makes every later step more likely to work. Detecting it gives your team a chance to warn the specific people who are being studied.
howItWorks: Your identity provider records directory searches and profile views, including the account and the search terms.
The rule counts those searches per account over a period of time.
It compares the count with what is normal for that person's role, such as a recruiter or a help desk agent.
It also looks at web requests to people search and professional networking sites from corporate devices.
It checks email gateway logs for messages or lookups that walk through many staff addresses in sequence.
Accounts or sources that go far beyond the normal pattern are grouped and raised for the security team.
beginner.example: Think of a hospital sign in sheet at the staff entrance. A visitor signs in once and goes to see one patient. That is normal. Another visitor signs in and then asks the receptionist for every nurse on the night shift. They also ask for the phone numbers. The receptionist would not hand that over and would remember the request. This detection watches for that request. It does not matter whether the request comes from outside the building or from an account inside.
takeaways: Names and job titles are the raw material of convincing phishing, so collecting them is a real event.
You must know which roles legitimately search the directory heavily, or they will drown the alert.
A role based alert lets you warn the exact people being researched, which is often more useful than blocking.

objectives: Explain how role information supports targeting in phishing and impersonation attacks
Identify identity provider and directory telemetry that records search and profile view activity
Establish a normal search volume per role using historical directory activity
Detect bulk enumeration of staff records by a single account or external source
Separate recruiting, sales and help desk activity from suspicious collection patterns
Convert a role reconnaissance alert into targeted warning and awareness actions
dataSources: Identity provider audit logs recording directory search queries, profile views and the authenticated account performing them
Corporate directory or lightweight directory access protocol query logs showing returned record counts and requested attributes
Secure web gateway logs for requests to professional networking and people search domains from corporate devices
Email gateway and phishing filter logs recording directory harvesting attempts and address verification behaviour
Human resources or recruiting system records used as a baseline of which accounts are expected to run bulk people searches
logic: The detection compares directory and people search activity with the expected behaviour for the account and role. The fields to correlate are the authenticated account, the identity provider group membership, the query text or attribute filter, the number of records returned, and the source address or device. The malicious pattern is one account returning far more records than its role needs, querying for sensitive combinations such as job title plus department plus manager, or an external source resolving many staff addresses in sequence. The benign case is a recruiter or sales representative running people searches as part of their job, or a help desk agent looking up a single user to answer a ticket. The decisive differences are the count of records touched, whether the query shape explores the organisation chart, and whether the account's role gives any reason to do so.
pseudoQuery:
# title: Bulk Employee Directory Enumeration Beyond Expected Role Volume
# logsource:
#   product: azure
#   service: audit
# detection:
#   selection:
#     operation|contains:
#       - 'Search directory'
#       - 'List users'
#   filter_expected_roles:
#     actor_group|contains:
#       - 'recruiting'
#       - 'helpdesk'
#   filter_baseline:
#     result_count|lt: 50
#   condition: selection and not filter_expected_roles and not filter_baseline
# level: low
falsePositives: Recruiting and talent acquisition staff searching professional networking sites and the internal directory for candidates
Sales and business development teams researching contacts at customer or partner organisations
Identity governance reviews in which administrators list user attributes across large groups for an access certification campaign
Automated human resources or onboarding systems that query the directory when creating or updating staff accounts
tuningNotes: Establish a per role baseline of directory search volume from at least one month of history before enabling the rule, and express the threshold as a count of returned records or distinct users rather than a count of search actions. Maintain filters for recruiting, sales and identity administration groups, sourced from the identity provider group membership so that they follow staff changes automatically. Scope the first release to queries that request manager, job title or contact attributes across many users, which is the shape of organisation chart collection. Excluding expected roles costs you visibility into a compromised recruiter account, so add a companion rule that alerts when an account in an allowed group searches from a new device or outside its normal working hours.
